title: Protein-Protein Interaction Networks in Solanum tuberosum Using TurboID Proximity Labeling
author: Shi, Marti Ferrando, et al.
materials: Thermo Scientific Pierce Streptavidin Magnetic Beads
Trans-Blot Turbo Mini PVDF Transfer Packs
One Shot TOP10 Chemically Competent E. coli cells

steps.title: Electroporate Agrobacterium with TurboID plasmid
steps.instruction: Transform 100 ng TurboID plasmid into 20 µL electro‑competent Agrobacterium, electroporate, recover and plate colonies.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 ng plasmid to 20 µL electro‑competent Agrobacterium in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Transfer the mixture to a pre‑chilled 0.2 cm electroporation cuvette.
Pulse at 1.4 kV using a MicroPulser Electroporator.
Add 0.25 mL YEB (or LB) medium to the cuvette, mix gently, and transfer the cells to a clean 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate 2 h at 28 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Plate 20–50 µL on LB agar plates (90 mm diameter) containing the appropriate antibiotics (C58C1: Rifampicin, Tetracycline, Kanamycin; AGL1: Chloramphenicol, Carbenicillin, Kanamycin).
Incubate plates until colonies appear (typically 30–60 colonies).

steps.title: Grow starter Agrobacterium culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single transformed colony and grow a starter culture for two days.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate the colony into 10 mL LB medium with the same antibiotics used for selection.
Incubate for 2 days at 28 °C with continuous shaking at 200 rpm.
Optional: Verify the construct by colony PCR using 5 µL of culture with primers P35S‑CaMV‑Fw and YFP‑Rv (or gene‑specific reverse primer), then send the PCR product for Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Scale up Agrobacterium with induction agents
steps.instruction: Transfer the starter culture to a 250 mL flask containing YEB, antibiotics, acetosyringone and MES, then incubate for one day.

substeps.instruction: Add the 10 mL starter culture to a 250 mL flask containing YEB medium with the appropriate antibiotics.
Supplement the medium with acetosyringone to a final concentration of 200 µM and MES solution 1 to a final concentration of 10 mM.
Incubate for 1 day at 28 °C with continuous shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells to target OD
steps.instruction: Collect Agrobacterium cells, resuspend in MMA buffer to OD600 0.3–0.4, and prepare co‑infiltration mixes if needed.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture at 3,000 × g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in freshly prepared MMA buffer, adjusting the suspension to an OD600 of 0.3–0.4.
For co‑infiltration of two constructs, mix the two Agrobacterium suspensions in a 1:1 ratio.
Typical volume: 30–50 mL culture is sufficient for infiltrating 3–5 leaves; on average 1 mL suspension per leaf.

steps.title: Incubate suspension before infiltration
steps.instruction: Incubate the Agrobacterium suspension in MMA for 1–2 h at 20–25 °C in the dark without shaking.

steps.title: Infiltrate potato leaves with Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: Fully infiltrate 3–5 leaves per plant using a 1 mL needleless syringe and maintain plants under controlled conditions.

substeps.instruction: Optionally water the potato plants 1–2 h before infiltration to open stomata.
Optionally make a small scratch on the lower epidermis of each leaf with a needle or scalpel to facilitate infiltration.
Using a 1 mL needleless syringe, infiltrate the suspension from the lower side of each leaf until fully saturated.
Change gloves between different construct infiltrations to avoid cross‑contamination.
After infiltration, keep plants in a greenhouse at 18–22 °C under long‑day lighting.

steps.title: Extract total protein from leaf tissue
steps.instruction: Lyse infiltrated leaves in RIPA buffer with inhibitors, clarify, and adjust volume for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Grind leaf tissue and add 2 mL RIPA buffer per gram of tissue, supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail and MG‑132 (final concentration as specified in Materials).
Keep the samples on ice and vortex‑mix for a total of 15 min, vortexing intermittently while maintaining the samples on ice.
Centrifuge the lysates for 30 min at 4 °C at maximum speed (≈17,000 × g).
Transfer the clear supernatant to a pre‑cooled V‑shaped 15 mL tube.
Adjust each sample to a final volume of 10 mL with RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitor cocktail and MG‑132.
Use LoBind tubes for all subsequent steps.
Note: Each Cytiva Life Sciences PD‑10 desalting column holds 2.5 mL; therefore, four columns are required per 10 mL sample.
